title: Visakhapatnam LG Polymers Gas Leak 2020
summary: Styrene vapour leaked from a storage tank at LG Polymers India, Vishakhapatnam on 7 May 2020. The leak occurred early morning when plant was under restart after COVID-19 lockdown. Inadequate post-shutdown inspection, degraded safety barriers, and absence of continuous gas monitoring at perimeter were key precursors. 11 fatalities, 1000+ affected.

title: Coke Oven Flash Fire, Bhilai Steel Plant 2017
summary: A flash fire occurred in the coke oven battery area at Bhilai Steel Plant (SAIL) when a hot-work permit was issued without adequate gas testing. CO concentration was above 50ppm at the work site. Fire suppression system in the area was under maintenance and offline. Two workers sustained burn injuries.

source: CSB Investigation Report (public), Clairton Coke Works PA 2018
title: Clairton Coke Works Fire, Pennsylvania 2018
summary: A fire at U.S. Steel Clairton Coke Works damaged desulfurization equipment after a plant upset. The fire knocked out flue gas treatment, causing SO2 and CO emissions. The incident highlighted inadequate emergency shutdown procedures, degraded ventilation in affected zones, and permit-to-work system failures during upset conditions.
outcome: equipment damage, prolonged emissions, community impact

title: Near-Miss: Gas Accumulation with Active Hot-Work Permit, Zone 2
summary: [SYNTHETIC - schema-matched to AccidentPath] CO concentration rose to 180ppm in Zone 2 (coke oven charging area) during a routine shift. A hot-work permit was active for welding on an adjacent conveyor. The shift officer noticed the gas reading before ignition occurred and suspended the permit. Ventilation fan in Zone 2 was operating at 55% capacity due to a partial blockage.

title: Near-Miss: PPE Non-Compliance in Gas-Affected Zone with Permit Active
summary: [SYNTHETIC] A gas sensor alarm triggered in Zone 1 (pushing area) at 210ppm CO. A hot-work permit was active for maintenance nearby. Three workers were found without supplied-air respirators. The zone was evacuated before any exposure injury. Post-incident review found the permit PTW checklist had not been signed off for gas monitoring.

title: Near-Miss: Ventilation Fan Failure in Occupied Coke Oven Zone
summary: [SYNTHETIC] Main ventilation fan in Zone 3 (by-product plant) failed during a 14:00 shift. Airflow dropped to 38% nominal within 20 minutes. Five workers were present. The DCS alarm was acknowledged but no immediate evacuation order was issued. A second sensor then detected rising H2S at 8ppm. Workers self-evacuated without injury after 12 minutes.

title: Near-Miss: Equipment Failure with Worker in Zone, Rotating Machinery
summary: [SYNTHETIC] A cooling water pump impeller in Zone 5 (cooling tower area) developed a crack under vibration. The predictive maintenance system flagged failure probability at 0.72. One maintenance worker was in the zone performing an unrelated inspection. The zone supervisor was alerted and the worker was evacuated 4 minutes before the pump seized and casing cracked.

title: Near-Miss: Fire Suppression Offline During Hot-Work with Rising Gas
summary: [SYNTHETIC] A hot-work permit was issued in Zone 1 for gasket replacement on a coke oven door. Unknown to the permit issuer, the fire suppression sprinkler system in Zone 1 had been isolated for maintenance 48 hours earlier and the isolation had not been lifted. CO readings rose to 155ppm during the work. The hot-work was stopped when an operator noticed the sprinkler isolation tag on a nearby valve.

title: Near-Miss: Multiple Factors Compound — Gas, PPE, Vent, Active Permit
summary: [SYNTHETIC] The canonical HE-042 scenario: CO at 235ppm in Zone 2, hot-work permit active, ventilation at 52% nominal, two workers without respirators. The compound rule engine (CAUSALCUT equivalent in this plant) triggered alarm. Zone supervisor suspended the permit and evacuated workers within 3 minutes. No ignition occurred.
oisd_clause: OISD-STD-105 S7.3; OISD-STD-105 S8.1; OISD-STD-114 S4.2

title: Near-Miss: Gas Accumulation in Unoccupied Zone — Late Detection
summary: [SYNTHETIC] CO accumulated to 310ppm in Zone 4 (oven battery end) over 45 minutes during night shift. The zone was unoccupied. A routine patrol detected the reading. Root cause: a standby ventilation fan had not been switched on after primary fan maintenance. The gas accumulation was cleared by switching on the standby fan.

title: Near-Miss: Barrier Degradation — Fire Suppression Overdue for Proof Test
summary: [SYNTHETIC] A quarterly proof test audit revealed that the fire suppression system in Zone 3 had not been proof-tested for 7 months (interval: 6 months). The system had also accumulated 3 demand events (alarm activations) since last test. The system was classified impaired. Hot-work permits in Zone 3 were suspended pending barrier restoration.
outcome: impaired barrier detected, proactive suspension of permits

source: HSE UK Investigation (public), Coke Oven Benzene Exposure 2015
title: UK Coke Oven Benzene Over-Exposure Incident 2015
summary: UK Health and Safety Executive investigated chronic benzene over-exposure at a coke works. Workers in the coal charging and pushing areas were exposed to benzene concentrations exceeding WEL (Workplace Exposure Limit) over multiple shifts. Inadequate LEV (local exhaust ventilation), no continuous atmospheric monitoring, and non-compliance with respiratory PPE requirements were identified as root causes.
